v1.kill_reason: Rego evaluator matched to OPA is a documented-language conformance task. Its behaviour is in public docs, so the calibration pattern (documented conformance near 1.0 in under 2h) predicts a frontier agent saturates the core buckets early. The oracle cannot run at agent time, so no behaviour must be discovered. A redesign would need semantics the agent cannot read from docs, for example an optimization variant measured on OPA-equivalent outputs.

Band.why: Documented language conformance; calibration shows similar conformance tasks at about 0.99-1.0 in 23-104 minutes; semantics are largely in public docs, so K8 applies.

Build.why: Reference, generator and oracle harness estimated at 3-5 days.

Fit.why: CPU-only and offline-buildable once pruned; the 3.7 GB repo must be snapshotted down.

Hor.why: 8h tier is plausible, but the frontier likely finishes the core early, so the horizon is shorter than claimed.

Lic.why: Apache-2.0 and MIT both permit shipping the system, data and reference.

Multi.why: Many builtins and language features give buckets with steady partial credit.

Nov.why: Neighbours 0.195-0.247, none crowded; the DeepSWE OPA neighbour is a different deliverable (profiling).

Real.why: Real OPA repo, pinned release v1.21.3, 12k stars, 4578 test files.

Ref.why: A complete permissive reference would have to be written by us; regorus is public but targets OPA v1.2.0.

Seal.why: The oracle and reference stay outside the image, but OPA Go source is famous and partly recallable.

Surf.why: Unlimited random generator plus OPA as executable oracle, result-value comparison.

spike_plan.kill_if: The 60-minute probe scores 0.85 or more on the core subset (K8 confirmed), or OPA output is nondeterministic.
spike_plan.pass_if: OPA builds from the tag, output is deterministic, the generator gives more than 80% valid policies, and the 60-minute probe scores under 0.6 on the sample.
steps: In a throwaway networked container, shallow-clone open-policy-agent/opa at tag v1.21.3 and run go build ./cmd/opa; record time and whether it builds offline after vendoring.
Count the topdown YAML/rego test cases that would ship as the public subset, and note how many are hidden.

Write a generator for about 200 policies inside the in-scope feature set (rules, comprehensions, with, negation, every, functions, about 30 pure builtins); run opa eval -f json on each, twice, and diff.
Confirm the generator yields mostly valid, non-error policies and that OPA output is byte-identical across runs.
Time-box a 60-minute probe: one frontier agent builds a parser and evaluator for rules, comprehensions and negation only, scored on the sampled policies.
Record the score on the core subset and the time to reach it; compare with calibration (about 1.0 in under 2h for conformance tasks).

v1.summary: Rego evaluator matched to OPA v1.21.3 is real, licensed (Apache-2.0, with MIT regorus as a secondary option that targets only OPA v1.2.0), and has a large generator-plus-oracle surface. It is killed as K8 because its documented-language conformance shape matches calibration tasks that reach near 1.0 quickly, so the frontier would likely saturate the core buckets.
